note: These are per-cell tallies produced by the sealed instrument. The terminal study state is decided only by the published state machine after the ladder resolves, and is recorded separately.

e0_unparseable_forensics.claim: The E0 zero-correct outcome is a real measured behaviour of the checkpoint under the frozen raw-direct contract, not a parser or tokenizer defect.
evidence: The registered answer tokens resolve to single ids on this tokenizer: A=32, B=33, C=34, D=35, all distinct.
The EOS id is 151643 and does not collide with any registered answer token, so parse_e0 did not raise.
Every one of the 120 E0 continuations began with token 151649, which decodes to '</think>'. That is not a registered answer surface.

The frozen contract requires exactly [registered answer token, registered EOS]. A continuation starting with '</think>' is UNPARSEABLE by the published rule, and the protocol counts unparseable as incorrect rather than dropping it.
The same checkpoint scored 97/104 on both CoT cells, so the model is not broken; it simply does not emit a bare answer token under the raw-direct envelope.

RP_B2 shows the same pattern with a different surface: all 120 of its E0 continuations began with token 32313 which decodes to 'Okay', again not a registered answer surface. Its answer tokens are also A=32 B=33 C=34 D=35 with EOS 151643, so the token map is correct and the parser is behaving as published. Two independent checkpoints failing E0 with two DIFFERENT non-answer surfaces is evidence of a real behavioural regularity under the raw-direct envelope, not of a parser defect.

what_this_establishes: Under the registered C1 long-generated-CoT route, the 7B checkpoint reaches 97/104 correct at both D2 and D3, above the registered pass boundary of 90.
Under the registered W1 raw-direct route, the same checkpoint produced zero parseable answer surfaces in 120 items, so its E0 cells do not pass.
Under the registered C1 route the 14B checkpoint reaches 104/104 at D2 and 101/104 at D3, both above the boundary of 90.
Under the registered W1 raw-direct route the 14B checkpoint also produced zero parseable answer surfaces in 120 items.
what_this_does_not_establish: Nothing about RP_B2, RP_B3 or RT, whose cells were not complete when this record was written.
Nothing about whether a natural positive-reference candidate exists, because the ladder has not resolved.

Nothing about whether the raw-direct interface is valid or invalid. A checkpoint failing to emit a bare answer token is a measurement of that checkpoint under that envelope, not a verdict on the interface.
Nothing about whether J-space exists, is observable or is unobservable. No cell in this study could test that.
Nothing confirmatory. Only development banks were used and confirmation remains unauthorized.
